content.text:
Three classes directly declare `implements Cache<K, V>` in `guava/src` (excluding android/ and tests):

1. **`com.google.common.cache.AbstractCache<K, V>`** — `public abstract class AbstractCache<K, V> implements Cache<K, V>`
2. **`com.google.common.cache.ForwardingCache<K, V>`** — `public abstract class ForwardingCache<K, V> extends ForwardingObject implements Cache<K, V>`
3. **`com.google.common.cache.LocalCache.LocalManualCache<K, V>`** (a static nested class inside `LocalCache.java`) — `static class LocalManualCache<K, V> implements Cache<K, V>, Serializable`

Note: `LocalCache` itself implements `ConcurrentMap<K, V>`, not `Cache`; and `LocalLoadingCache` extends `LocalManualCache` rather than declaring `implements Cache` itself, so it doesn't count as a direct implementer.

ANSWER: Three classes directly implement `Cache<K, V>` in guava/src (excluding android/ and tests): `com.google.common.cache.AbstractCache`, `com.google.common.cache.ForwardingCache`, and the nested static class `LocalCache.LocalManualCache` (in LocalCache.java).
